newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bernheim-Comofi plans merger of units with Befimmo.
newsitem.headline: Bernheim-Comofi plans merger of units with Befimmo.

text.p: Belgian property company firm and car park operator Bernheim-Comofi said on Thursday it was planning to sell new shares in real estate fund Befimmo.

The new shares would be issued under plans to merge Befimmo with five other companies Bernheim-Comofi acquired from Swedish property group Prifast earlier this year. The merger is due to be decided at an extraordinary shareholders meeting at the end of the summer, Bernheim said in a statement.
Bernheim said the merger would boost Befimmo's portfolio value by 3.3 billion francs and cut its stake to 54 percent.
"(Bernheim-Comofi) is planning a Public offer for the sale of new Befimmo shares issued at the merger and giving the right to participate in profits from October 1, 1997," it said.
It said about 60 percent of the offer will be reserved for existing shareholders.
Bernheim-Comofi said it would renounce its own preferential rights.
The operation could be worth 3.4 billion francs, it said.
